To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in men, testosterone levels are negatively associated with insulin levels and glucose levels, and estradiol to testosteron (E/T) ratio is positively associated with these levels, 2) in men, these associations are independent of body mass index (a marker of obesity), 3) in women, testosterone levels are positively associated with glucose and insulin levels, and estradial to testosterone (E/T) is negatively associated with these levels.
in men with obesity, testosterone correlates negatively and E/T correlates positively with insulin and glucose levels.
in obese men, as in non-obese, serum testosterone level correlated inversely and the E/T ratio correlated positively with insulin and glucose levels and with the I/G ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of sex hormones, particularly testosterone, in the development of the glucose-insulin and lipid disorders that are risk factors for CHDs.
the relationship between the sex hormone milieu and the glucose-insuline-lipid (GIL) defect in obesity, a risk factor for CHD.
the relationship between serum sex hormones, glucose-insulin-lipsis (GIL) metabolism and the risk factors for coronary heart disease in men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relationships between sex hormones and insulin, glucose, and I/G in obese men are similar to those in non-obese, but that the relationships between E/T and cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, blood pressure, and W/H are different.
the relationship between sex hormones and the risk factors for CHDs are not independent of BMI and age.
the sex hormone milieu of obese men is altered in the same manner as in non-obese and that this alteration may be a factor in the development of the glucose-insulin and lipid disorders of obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity is a risk factor for coronary heart disease (CVD) and its risk factor in men.
obesity is a state of hyperestrogenemia and hypotestosteronia, and that this hormonal milieu may be related to hyperglycemia and hyperinsulinemia.
obesity, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes mellitus are associated with low serum testosterone and high serum estradiol, which may contribute to the pathophysiology of the metabolic syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a relationship between the sex hormones, obesity, and the glucose/insulin/lipid defect.
there are many factors that influence testosterone levels.
there is an association between low levels of testosterone and obesity, and that this association is mediated by insulin and glucose.
